requirements.evidence: CreateQueue/UpdateQueue implement trimming, slugging, per-entity uniqueness and QueryException race mapping (app/Actions/CreateQueue.php:15-57; app/Actions/UpdateQueue.php:14-78); SetQueueAccess implements upsert/revoke, validation and audit logs (app/Actions/SetQueueAccess.php:15-75); QueuePolicy has create/update/manageAccess/call and both call paths authorize (app/Policies/QueuePolicy.php:18-81; app/Actions/CallNextTicket.php:29-32; app/Models/Ticket.php:90-110); the migration, model, factory and docs match the contract.

conventions.evidence: Domain writes stay in app/Actions and authorize through policies; QueueAccess uses #[Fillable] and an array cast (app/Models/QueueAccess.php:10-26); the migration is reversible; docs/business-rules.md, docs/database-schema.md and CHANGELOG.md are updated. Deviation: the new public __invoke methods have no PHPDoc (app/Actions/CreateQueue.php:15; app/Actions/UpdateQueue.php:14; app/Actions/SetQueueAccess.php:15), although the conventions ask for PHPDoc on touched public methods.

security.evidence: Every write path calls Gate::forUser(...)->authorize (CreateQueue.php:17, UpdateQueue.php:16, SetQueueAccess.php:17, CallNextTicket.php:32, Ticket.php:103). SetQueueAccess validates every permission value against the enum (SetQueueAccess.php:25-35); QueuePolicy rejects non-array permissions and requires call for non-managers (QueuePolicy.php:46-72); mass assignment is guarded by #[Fillable], and no UI/escaping surface was added.

tests.evidence: tests/Feature/QueueManagementTest.php:1-294 covers create/update, per-entity slug conflicts, authorization denial, grant/revoke and audit logs, corrupted permissions, factory entity consistency, and both call paths; tests/Feature/CallNextTicketTest.php:18-21 and the following hunks add manager memberships. Missing: a positive CallNextTicket test for an employee holding a call grant, and an explicit partial-update (null = unchanged) case.

simplicity.evidence: Actions are small and direct, but the same isUniqueViolation helper is duplicated in app/Actions/CreateQueue.php:59-68 and app/Actions/UpdateQueue.php:80-89, and the same slug validation message is repeated.

readability.evidence: Names and methods are clear and follow sibling style (app/Policies/QueuePolicy.php:18-81; app/Actions/SetQueueAccess.php:15-75). Nits: unused $owner in tests/Feature/QueueManagementTest.php:186 and a test name at :268 that promises an inactive-first check the body does not perform.

scope.evidence: The diff is limited to queue actions/policy/model/migration/factory, the two call paths, docs and tests; no queue delete/remove action or UI was added, and the out-of-scope items in task.md remain untouched.

issues.explanation: The isUniqueViolation helper and its duplicate-slug validation message are copied in both actions; one shared implementation would prevent them from diverging.

isUniqueViolation treats every SQLSTATE 23000 as a duplicate slug, so an unrelated integrity or foreign-key failure would be reported as a slug ValidationException instead of surfacing the real error.
The new public __invoke methods have no PHPDoc, although the project conventions ask for PHPDoc on public methods touched; the QueuePolicy methods do document themselves.

CallNextTicket is tested for denial on every mode and for a manager success path, but not for an employee with a call grant actually calling a ticket; that positive path is only exercised through Ticket::call.

The revoke path selects the row and then deletes it; if another request deletes it in between, the action still logs queue.access.revoked even though its delete affected no row, which is the case the task says must not be logged.
The $owner assignment is never used in the self-grant denial test and should be removed.
The test name says it checks inactive-first behavior on Ticket::call, but its body only checks the employee grant success; the inactive check is in the next test.

review.summary: The change implements the queue lifecycle, per-queue access grants, the QueuePolicy, and authorization on both call paths, with a matching migration, docs and a broad Pest test suite. It is close to approvable; the main review points are a duplicated unique-violation helper, a small revoke/log race, missing PHPDoc on the new actions, and a few test gaps and nits.
